Q: How do I use Homebrew installed Python as the default Python? A:

python formula now uses python3 (v3.6.5 for now), and Homebrew will link the directory:

/usr/local/opt/python -> ../Cellar/python/3.6.5

It will also link the binary:

/usr/local/bin/python3 -> ../Cellar/python/3.6.5/bin/python3

If you still need to use python2.x, use:

brew install python@2

To use Homebrew's python, just put its directory in PATH. For Bash:

export PATH="/usr/local/opt/python/libexec/bin:$PATH"

For Fish:

set -x PATH /usr/local/opt/python/libexec/bin $PATH

Note:

  1. doing this will shadow the system default version of python
  2. Homebrew used to link python to /usr/local/share/python in older versions.

Q: Is Java still worth learning to get a job soon? Seniors — please spit the truth A:

Regardless of the language, you're going to have a bad time right now looking for a job as a junior dev. But you will have a worse time if you only know one language. If you can prove that you can work with several languages you are showing ability to learn and adapt.

The best asset in job hunting is having friends and acquaintances who already have jobs in the field you want to work in.

Q: Error running gluonfx:compile produces: $JAVA_HOME and $GRAALVM_HOME are undefined A:

The problem is:

The user xxx executes mybashrc to defines the 2 environment variables

While,

root executes sudo mvn gluonfx:compile which has no access to environment variables defined by xxx

removing sudo executes mvn glunfx:compile as xxx

Q: How to reduce indentation level of argument help in argparse? A:

Continuing from @wkl's excellent answer:

ArgumentParser takes the formatter_class keyword argument, which expects a class and not an instantiated object. Argparse's formatter classes have the max_help_position kwarg, which is exactly what we want, but because we don't instantiate the class we don't get a chance to set it.

This is exactly the situation partial is for:

import argparse
from functools import partial

partial_formatter = partial(
    argparse.HelpFormatter, 
    max_help_position=10
)

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
    formatter_class=partial_formatter
)

partial returns a callable object that calls the wrapped method but substitutes specific arguments. The object has the same prototype as the wrapped function. It's exactly the right fit here, since we don't want to involve ourselves with argparse's other internals (like tracking prog) with a lambda.

More concisely:

import argparse
from functools import partial

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
    formatter_class=partial(argparse.HelpFormatter, max_help_position=10)
)

Did you try brew link --overwrite python?

Q: Taiwanese language and country codes A:

zh-TW = Traditional Chinese for Taiwan specifically (BCP 47 region subtag) zh-Hant = Traditional Chinese script broadly (Taiwan + Hong Kong + Macau) zh-CHT = Old Microsoft tag, not standard BCP 47 — avoid it. Your ES-419 analogy is perfect: zh-Hant is the "ES-419 of Traditional Chinese" — it's the broad umbrella, while zh-TW/zh-HK/zh-MO are the region-specific variants. For your site: use zh-Hant as primary, then region subtags if you need local differences (date formats, vocabulary).
